ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Approx. 0.65 low-intensity (black) to 0.35 high-intensity (white) across the visible ventral surface area.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Dominant low-intensity central zone originating from the peduncle and radiating outward into both lobes. High-intensity (white) zones occupy the distal 40% of the lobe area, characterized by a transition zone of radial, low-intensity filamental striations projecting toward the trailing edge.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Distinct V-shaped notch with an internal vertex angle of approximately 55 degrees; notch depth constitutes roughly 15% of the total vertical fluke height.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Asymmetrical topography. The left lobe (viewer perspective) trailing edge features three significant macro-notches (approx. 5-10 pixel depth). The right lobe trailing edge exhibits higher-frequency, lower-amplitude micro-serrations (approx. 2-4 pixel depth) along the boundary.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Convex leading edge curvature from peduncle attachment to the acute distal tips; trailing edges follow a shallow concave sweep toward the central notch.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Localized high-intensity pixel clusters concentrated at the distal tips of both lobes, appearing as roughly circular focal points (barnacle colonization/scars).
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Several faint, vertical, high-intensity linear interruptions (rake marks) are visible traversing the low-intensity pigmentation on the inner mid-section of the left lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Notable irregular trauma/excision (large notch) on the trailing edge of the left lobe, approximately one-third of the distance from the median notch to the tip.
other_distinctive_markers: Symmetrical radial 'burst' pigmentation pattern where the central black field meets the white peripheral fields.
